chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Chapter 462: The Lotus Seat – Li Huowang Fights a Twin Exorcism
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang struggles to purge rampaging Immortals from Bai Lingmiao and the Second Spirit using a sacred jade lotus that might erase them entirely.
og_title: The Lotus Seat: A Cure That Deletes the Patient
og_description: Li Huowang faces his cruelest choice yet: use an artifact that could destroy his loved ones to save them from the Immortals.
twitter_title: A jade lotus that purges the evil—and the self.
twitter_description: Li Huowang must use a White Lotus relic that nearly erases Bai Lingmiao to save her from possession.

lore_anchors.definition: A ritual practitioner who self-mutilates to prove a spirit’s presence; the body becomes a vessel and gains temporary immunity to pain.
The “Second Spirit” assistant in a chuma ritual; often a silent, possessed entity that can act independently from the Lead Spirit.
A historical Chinese secret religious tradition; in the novel, it is a hereditary cult within the Bai family with real supernatural power.
A Buddhist-aligned relic that purges possessing entities; its power to define “impurity” is so absolute it can erase the self.
A talisman-bearing bamboo sliver used to enhance or track a messenger animal.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does the jade lotus nearly erase the Second Spirit?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The lotus’s “purification” is absolute: it treats the possessed person’s soul as just another impurity to remove, not just the parasitic Immortal.
It’s a set of combat-oriented divine abilities inherited by White Lotus mediums, often involving inviting a spirit into the body for supernatural strength or resilience.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What did the Second Spirit mean by ‘the Immortals want to descend’?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The rampaging Immortals are attempting to use mortal bodies as permanent vessels to enter the mortal world, turning the Heavenly Calamity into an invasion.
